description: 👋 Hi, I'm Abel Biruktesfa 🇪🇹 A developer interested in cybersecurity, AI, software development, astronomy & space technology. 💻 I’ve worked on EthioSec Scanner, an AI-powered web security platform, AI/automation projects, web apps, and astronomy/aerospace challenges. 🚀 Looking for teammates skilled in UI/UX, AI/ML, data science, GIS, space science, research & presentation. 🌍🛰️
summary: AstroQuest Hub is a browser-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer where learners take command of a lunar outpost and discover that space exploration runs on decisions, not just rockets. Across six missions, from First Day at the Outpost to Outpost Emergency, cadets investigate evidence files, choose a strategy, watch the simulation play out and read a debrief that explains the science behind the result. The outpost never resets: power, oxygen, water, food and radiation protection carry from one mission to the next, so a hasty choice today makes tomorrow harder and no option is ever free. A Spacecraft Lab invites cadets to explore a crew module, and a Science Log collects every concept they meet. In the Solar Storm mission, the game loads real solar flare records from NASA's DONKI service and honestly labels any fallback as simulated. By turning real space-operations thinking into hands-on training, AstroQuest Hub teaches young people to weigh evidence and trade-offs before they act, and makes them curious to explore science, technology and engineering.
details:
AstroQuest Hub is an interactive, web-based space mission simulation platform designed as a junior astronaut training environment. It transforms foundational concepts in astronomy, astrophysics, and orbital mechanics into engaging, gamified mission modules. Through a standard web browser, users step into the role of astronaut trainees, progressing through structured scenarios that test their navigation, telemetry, and problem-solving skills while tracking their mission performance.
​By eliminating the need for specialized lab equipment or complex software installations, AstroQuest Hub makes aerospace education accessible and hands-on for students everywhere. Rather than relying on passive textbook reading, the platform encourages active decision-making in realistic space scenarios, helping learners visualize abstract scientific principles. Ultimately, the project aims to spark early curiosity in space exploration, aviation, and aerospace systems engineering among young learners.
​From a technical perspective, the platform is built using a modular frontend architecture powered by HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, allowing individual mission modules to be developed independently and seamlessly integrated into the main hub. The application was developed in Visual Studio Code, managed collaboratively through Git and GitHub for version control, and deployed for continuous browser accessibility.
